newsitem.title: USA: Lehman Brothers Q2 profits off from Q1.
newsitem.headline: Lehman Brothers Q2 profits off from Q1.

text.p: Lehman Brothers Holdings Inc said Thursday its second quarter profits slipped from first quarter levels, extending a trend among Wall Street firms.
Lehman's net earnings for the quarter totalled $121 million or $0.95 per share, down from the $144 million or $1.16 per share it earned in the first quarter.
Lehman's results improved versus a year ago, however, when it earned $108 million or $0.89 per share.
First half net income rose 25 percent to $265 million from $212 million.
"Overall, the first half of 1997 was a very good one for the firm," Richard Fuld, Lehman's chairman and chief executive said in a statement.

"Despite an extremely difficult trading and underwriting environment in March and April, the second quarter earnings reflect continued progress in building on Lehman Brothers' position as a leading global investment bank," he said.
Like many Wall Street firms, Lehman had its second quarter profits depressed by the sharp U.S. stock market downturn early in the quarter.
The market decline hit firms in several ways, particularly in the lucrative area of underwriting initial public offerings, which all but dried up in April.
Lehman is one of a handful of Wall Street firms whose fiscal quarters end in May instead of June, meaning they report earnings a month ahead of most of their competitors.

Among firms who have released figures, most have seen profits decline from the prior quarter, including Goldman Sachs & Co. Some, like A.G. Edwards Inc and Quick & Reilly, have also registered declines versus last year.

Morgan Stanley Dean Witter Discover & Co bucked the trend, however, announcing operating earnings Wednesday in its first reporting period as a combined firm that beat pro forma profits for the both first quarter and year-ago period.
